title: The Family Tree of Shapes
short: Place shapes in categories and subcategories.

blocks.html: In Grade 4 you sorted shapes by their sides and angles. Shapes also belong to families inside families, like a family tree: every square is a rectangle, and every rectangle is a quadrilateral.

A shape belongs to every category whose rules it meets. Categories nest: a smaller category (like squares) sits inside a bigger one (like rectangles) when every shape in it meets the bigger category's rules.

Each category is defined by its properties. A rectangle is a quadrilateral with 4 right angles. A square has 4 right angles, so it meets that rule: it is a rectangle, a special one that also has 4 equal sides. Being special does not take a shape out of the bigger family.

blocks.title: Most specific name
blocks.q: A quadrilateral has 4 equal sides but no right angles. What is its most specific name?
steps: 4 equal sides: it is a rhombus.
No right angles, so it is not a square.

blocks.title: Where two families meet
blocks.q: Which shapes are both rectangles and rhombuses?
steps: A rectangle has 4 right angles; a rhombus has 4 equal sides.
A shape with both is a square.

blocks.html: Thinking a shape can only have one name. A square is also a rectangle, a rhombus, a parallelogram and a quadrilateral. Check by testing the rules: does it have what that family requires?

Some books define a trapezoid as having exactly one pair of parallel sides, and others as having at least one pair. With the second definition, every parallelogram is also a trapezoid. Either way, the family-tree idea is the same.
